questions.question: Which of these substances can make it harder to drive?

options.text: Cough syrups and cold tablets with codeine or antihistamines.

questions.explanation: Many drugs can impair your driving. These include tranquilizers and sedatives, over-the-counter cough syrups, cold tablets, allergy medications that contain alcohol, codeine, or antihistamines, and illegal drugs.

questions.question: When driving in fog, what headlights should you use?
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, or snow. High beams reflect off the weather and make it harder to see.

questions.question: If your vehicle has a two-part safety belt system, what should you do?

options.text: Use both the lap and shoulder belts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the lap and shoulder belts.
questions.explanation: Wear both the lap belt and the shoulder belt. Using only one part greatly reduces your protection. If you have an automatic shoulder belt, also buckle your lap belt.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road ahead curves left then right.
The road ahead curves right then left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead curves right then left.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign tells drivers the road will curve right, then left. Slow down to safely navigate these curves.

questions.question: If a vehicle has airbags, what should you do about seat belts?

options.text: Seat belts should still be worn.
Seat belts do not need to be worn.
Seat belts should be worn behind the back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Seat belts should still be worn.
questions.explanation: Airbags are important safety devices. For best protection, use both lap and shoulder belts along with airbags.

questions.question: When does your reaction time become slower?
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reflexes and reaction time. It reduces your vision and makes you less alert. As you drink more, your judgment worsens and your driving skills decrease. You will have trouble judging distances, speeds, and the movement of other vehicles.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Reserved parking for persons with disabilities.

questions.explanation: This sign warns that two lanes of traffic going the same direction will soon become one lane.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Drive faster to reach your destination sooner.
Find a safe place to park and take a short nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find a safe place to park and take a short nap.
questions.explanation: Watch for signs of fatigue while driving. You are too tired to drive safely if you struggle to keep your eyes open, drift from your lane, or need to turn up the radio and roll down windows to stay awake. Find a safe place to park and rest.

questions.question: When can you pass another vehicle?

options.text: On a road with a solid line next to your lane.
On a road with a broken line next to your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a road with a broken line next to your lane.
questions.explanation: A broken line means you can cross to change lanes. When a broken yellow line is next to a solid yellow line, passing is allowed from the lane with the broken line, but not from the lane with the solid line. Only change lanes when it is safe.

questions.question: To make a right turn, where should you turn from?

options.text: Speed up to give vehicles behind you more room to pass.

questions.explanation: Turn from the lane closest to the direction you want to travel. Turn into the lane closest to the one you just left. This way, you cross the fewest lanes of traffic.

questions.question: What color are temporary signs in construction and maintenance work areas?
questions.explanation: All temporary signs in work zones have orange backgrounds with black writing and symbols.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The height from the road to a bridge or overpass.
The maximum height a vehicle can be in this state.
The maximum width of a vehicle on the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: The height from the road to a bridge or overpass.
questions.explanation: This is a low clearance warning sign. It shows the distance from the road surface to the bottom of a bridge or overpass. In this case, it is 12 feet 6 inches.

questions.question: What are blind spots?

options.text: Spots in your vision when you are tired.
Areas you cannot see in your vehicle's mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Areas you cannot see in your vehicle's mirrors.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, look over your shoulder. Check the areas near the rear corners of your vehicle. These areas are called blind spots because your mirrors cannot show them.

questions.question: When should you drive at the maximum posted speed limit?
questions.explanation: The posted speed limit is the fastest legal speed under ideal conditions. Drive at the same speed as surrounding traffic, up to this limit. Always drive at a safe speed.

questions.question: What is the only way to lower blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
questions.explanation: Only time will help your body get rid of alcohol. Eating, drinking, or other actions cannot speed this up.

questions.question: What headlights should you use when driving in fog?
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, or snow. High beams reflect off these conditions and make it harder to see.

questions.question: What should you use when daylight starts to fade?
questions.explanation: As daylight fades, turn on your low beams so others can see you. Use high beams only in open areas with no other drivers.

questions.question: What should you do if the road is wet or icy?
questions.explanation: Your tires will not grip a wet or icy road as well. You should slow down when the road is wet or icy.

questions.question: What does this signal mean?
questions.explanation: Bicyclists use hand and arm signals because they do not have turn signals. A left arm straight out means the rider is turning left.

questions.question: When should you adjust your rearview and side mirrors?

options.text: Whenever you need to use them.
Before you get into the car.

questions.explanation: Before you drive, adjust your seat, mirrors, and safety belt. Secure items in your vehicle. Do not adjust mirrors while your vehicle is moving.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: You should use cruise control near a railroad crossing to keep a steady speed.
You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger or stop sign tells you to.
You have the right-of-way at a railroad crossing and do not need to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger or stop sign tells you to.
questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when directed by a flagger, stop sign, or warning signal. Always be careful when driving near railroad tracks.

questions.question: You must obey instructions from school crossing guards:

options.text: Only if you see children present.

questions.explanation: Always watch for crossing guards near schools and always follow their instructions.

questions.question: If a traffic light is green and a police officer signals you to stop, you should:

options.text: Do what the vehicle in front of you does.

questions.explanation: Always obey a police officer's instructions, even if they conflict with traffic signals, signs, or road markings.

questions.question: You must yield to a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog:

options.text: Only when the guide dog is leading them across the street.
Only if a crossing guard is present.

questions.explanation: Always give the right-of-way to pedestrians using guide dogs or white canes, with or without a red tip.

questions.question: If you approach a stopped school bus with flashing lights and an extended signal arm, you should:

options.text: Proceed at 15 mph if no children are present.
Proceed at normal speed, but watch for children.

questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop when you see a school bus with flashing lights and an extended signal arm. Stay stopped until the arm retracts and the bus moves. This applies whether you are traveling in the same direction or from the opposite direction.
